input.project_card:
Idea (user's words): An appointment booking app for my family clinic in Indore: patients pick a doctor and a time slot, and the receptionist manages the day's schedule.
Category guess: clinic appointment booking. Geography: Indore, India. Mode: guided. Language: en. Situation: owner, not technical.
input.fact_digest:
FCT-001 [context|location] The business is a family clinic in Indore (from the first message)
FCT-002 [role|patients] Patients choose a doctor and a time slot (from the first message)
FCT-003 [role|reception] The receptionist manages the day's schedule (from the first message)

needs.label: How it earns money
needs.sufficient: Who pays whom for what, where the revenue comes from, and which parts are free versus paid.
option_labels: A small fee on each sale or booking
Free to use; the business pays for it

needs.label: Who it is for
needs.sufficient: At least one named segment: who they are, their main goal, and where and how they use the app. Separate the paying customer from the end user when they differ.

needs.label: Roles
needs.sufficient: Each distinct kind of person who signs in: their top goal and what they can approve or change.

needs.label: Features
needs.sufficient: What each feature is for (the job it does) and what must be in the first release.
option_labels: Search and browse a list of items

needs.label: Sensitive information
needs.sufficient: What sensitive information the app handles, such as health, financial, children's data or ID documents.

needs.label: How people sign in
needs.sufficient: How each kind of user signs in: phone number and code, email, a social account, or not at all.
option_labels: Phone number and a one-time code

needs.label: Services to connect
needs.sufficient: Which outside services to connect (payments, maps, SMS codes, push messages, email, identity checks) and what each is for.

needs.label: Tone and mood
needs.sufficient: Two or three words for the mood and personality the app should have.

needs.label: Country and city
needs.sufficient: Country; city or region (or nationwide); the languages spoken there; and whether it starts in one city or several.

style_notes: features: propose features as the job each one does, in the user's words.
roles: propose the roles you can already see and ask what each may approve or change.

business_model_candidates: a small booking fee per appointment

likely_features.name: Book a slot with a chosen doctor
Daily schedule for the reception desk
likely_features.intent: see and move the day's appointments

questions.intent: learn how doctors' time is organised (fixed slots, walk-ins or both)
unlocks: Blueprint: slot rules and the reception view
questions.answer_spec: Whether every doctor works on fixed slots, takes walk-ins, or both
questions.text: Do all your doctors see patients on fixed time slots, or do some also take walk-ins?
questions.why_we_ask: This decides how the booking screen and the reception view must behave.

options.label: Fixed slots for every doctor
options.description: Nobody is seen without a booking

options.label: A mix of booked slots and walk-ins
options.description: Some time is kept free for walk-ins
options.reason: Most family clinics keep some time free for people who walk in

options.label: Mostly walk-ins; bookings are few
options.description: The app would add a booking option

questions.recommended: A mix of booked slots and walk-ins

questions.intent: learn what happens when a patient does not turn up or cancels late
questions.answer_spec: The rule for a missed or late-cancelled slot, and whether any fee applies
questions.text: When a patient does not turn up or cancels at the last minute, what should happen to that slot?
questions.why_we_ask: Clinics handle this very differently, and the app has to follow your rule.
examples: e.g. the slot reopens after 15 minutes and the patient is reminded
e.g. no fee, but a note on the patient's record

questions.intent: learn who pays for the app: the clinic, the patient or neither
unlocks: Blueprint: whether payments are in scope
questions.answer_spec: Who pays whom for what, and which parts are free
questions.text: Who should pay for the booking side: the clinic, the patient, or is it just part of the consultation fee?
questions.why_we_ask: This decides whether the first version needs any payment screens.

options.label: The clinic pays; patients book free
options.reason: The clinic is the one that gains most from fewer missed visits

options.label: Patients pay a small booking fee
It is part of the consultation fee

questions.recommended: The clinic pays; patients book free

questions.intent: learn whether family members book on someone else's behalf
unlocks: Design: who the main screens are for
questions.answer_spec: The kinds of people who book, their goal and where they do it, and who pays versus who is seen
questions.text: Do patients always book for themselves, or do family members also book for children or parents?
questions.why_we_ask: It changes how a booking is attached to a person.
examples: e.g. mostly parents booking for children
e.g. adult children booking for elderly parents

questions.intent: learn which other people need to sign in
unlocks: Blueprint: roles and what each may change
questions.answer_spec: Each kind of person who signs in, their goal and what they can approve or change
questions.text: Besides you and the receptionist, who else needs to sign in?
questions.why_we_ask: Each kind of person gets their own view of the day.

options.label: Doctors, to see their own day

questions.intent: learn how much medical information the app will keep
unlocks: Blueprint: data model and access rules
questions.answer_spec: What sensitive information the app handles, such as health, financial or ID data
questions.text: Will the app keep anything about the visit itself, or only names and times?
questions.why_we_ask: Keeping medical details raises how carefully the data must be protected.

options.label: Only name, phone number and time
options.reason: Keeping less is simpler to start with

options.label: The reason for the visit as well

questions.recommended: Only name, phone number and time

questions.intent: learn the mood the booking experience should have
questions.answer_spec: Two or three words for the mood and personality of the app
questions.text: For your patients, which of these should booking feel like?

assumed_instead.assumption: Patients sign in with their phone number and a one-time code
assumed_instead.reason: Low risk and usual for appointment booking; shown for approval
Follows from the no-show question; confirmed after Q-002

expert_gaps: Reminder timing and who sends them
What the receptionist can override on a doctor's schedule
